headline: Raccoon Sightings Spark Nationwide Debate Over the 'Missing Thing'
deck: Suburban backyards become battlegrounds as raccoons claim lost territory; citizens demand answers, and local HOAs respond with sweeping bylaws.
article:
In a bizarre twist of fate, the Department of Raccoon Affairs has reported an alarming surge in raccoon sightings across the nation, as these masked marauders assert their claims over what they call 'lost territory.' Suburban communities, once tranquil, are now embroiled in a territorial dispute messier than a toddler's birthday cake.

Homeowners are scrambling to comply with the new mandate requiring them to report any raccoon encounters to their Homeowners' Associations, who are frantically drafting bylaws. These regulations may include hefty fines for those who fail to comply, with HOAs drawing inspiration from the murky legal precedent of 'Raccoon Rights' established in the 1973 case of Johnson v. Trashcan.

In a surprising development, a grassroots raccoon militia has emerged, boldly declaring themselves the champions of the 'Missing Thing'—a term that has become increasingly ambiguous as citizens debate whether it refers to the raccoons' territorial claims or the very essence of civility itself. "These raccoons are the true protectors of our rights!" proclaimed militia leader Edward J. Munchkin outside a local Taco Bell. "We demand official recognition and a seat at the governing table—or at least in the dumpster behind it!"

As the absurdity of a raccoon-led insurgency unfolds, experts speculate that future public policy may prioritize raccoon diplomacy, with some even suggesting a nationwide 'Raccoon Registry' to track sightings. Meanwhile, the existential question lingers: What exactly is the 'Missing Thing'—and should we even seek to uncover it?
author: Bertie H. Raccoonsworth, Senior Correspondent

oped.title: Raccoons: The True Victims of Suburban Hat Culture
oped.author: Bartholomew F. Snufflepuff, Self-Proclaimed Urban Wildlife Diplomate
oped.body: Ah, the great raccoon crisis of 2026! While suburbanites squabble over lost territory, I can’t help but ponder if the real culprits are not the raccoons, but the offensive hats worn by these so-called 'victims.' Clearly, the gaudy fedoras and neon visors are a magnet for raccoon ire! If we simply mandated a strict 'no hat' policy in our backyards, perhaps the raccoons would cease their trespasses. Imagine the peace as raccoons reclaim their rightful dominion! And let’s not forget the HOA, which is clearly overstepping by introducing bylaws instead of addressing the root cause: hat provocation. Join me in this noble pursuit of raccoon appeasement—after all, in a world where granaries are lawless and cats plot against our groceries, fashion is clearly our greatest threat!

stories.headline: Institute of Raccoon Behavior Releases Groundbreaking Study on Garbage Can Tactics
stories.deck: Findings may finally explain why your trash has never been safer.
stories.article:
In a remarkable revelation, the Institute of Raccoon Behavior has published a report detailing the ingenious strategies raccoons employ during their garbage can raids. The study found that 98% of raccoons surveyed prefer to work in pairs, utilizing the classic distraction-and-swipe technique. Surprisingly, the report also noted a rise in raccoon-proof technology among trash cans, with models now featuring advanced latches and decoy sounds.

Experts suggest that these developments in raccoon tactics may soon compel human engineers to devise even more sophisticated barriers. One engineer quipped, "If we can just keep the raccoons from commandeering our leftovers, we might finally achieve snack time utopia—or at least avoid snacks being hurled back at us."
